content:
You can align table captions to the left without using the caption package by redefining the `\@makecaption` command. Here are several methods:

## Method 1: Redefine \@makecaption (Simplest)

Add this to your preamble:

```latex
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \raggedright #1: #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother
```

## Method 2: With proper spacing and formatting

This version maintains better spacing and formatting:

```latex
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    \raggedright #1: #2\par
  \else
    \global \@minipagefalse
    \hb@xt@\hsize{\box\@tempboxa\hfil}%
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother
```

## Method 3: Using array package's \firsthline

If you're using the array package, you can do:

```latex
\usepackage{array}
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \begin{flushleft}#1: #2\end{flushleft}
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother
```

## Complete Example

Here's a complete working example:

```latex
\documentclass{article}

\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \raggedright #1: #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
Column 1 & Column 2 & Column 3 \\
\hline
Data 1 & Data 2 & Data 3 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\caption{This is a left-aligned caption for the table that can span multiple lines if needed}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

The `\makeatletter` and `\makeatother` commands are necessary because `\@makecaption` contains the @ symbol, which is normally not allowed in command names.
